objective: Explain diffusion and the factors that affect its rate.
success: Define diffusion using net movement and concentration gradient.
Name three factors that change the rate of diffusion and say which way each one changes it.
Apply diffusion to a real example in the body and to the model shown, keeping the two apart.
vocabulary: The net movement of particles from a higher concentration to a lower concentration.
How many particles of a substance there are in a given volume.
The difference in concentration between two places. Particles diffuse down it.
The overall movement once movement in both directions has been counted.
Needing no energy from the cell; diffusion is passive.
The total area available for particles to cross.
A thin layer that particles must cross, such as a cell membrane.
One of the tiny air sacs in the lungs where oxygen enters the blood. Plural: alveoli.
How fast something happens; here, how quickly particles move across.
facts: Particles move randomly all the time. Diffusion is the net result of that random movement, not a push.
Three factors raise the rate of diffusion: a steeper concentration gradient, a higher temperature and a larger surface area. A shorter distance to cross also raises it.
Diffusion needs no energy from the cell. Movement against a gradient using energy is active transport, a different process.
In the lungs, oxygen diffuses from the air in an alveolus into the blood; carbon dioxide diffuses the other way. The alveolus wall is one cell thick.
model_caption: A particle model of diffusion across a membrane. Particles are drawn far larger and fewer than the real thing, and the membrane is drawn as a line. This is an explanatory model, not a measurement of any real gas.
examples: Diffusion: oxygen into the blood at the alveoli; carbon dioxide out of a respiring cell; a smell spreading across a room.
Not diffusion: glucose pumped into a root hair against its gradient (active transport); water across a partially permeable membrane (osmosis, a special case treated in the next lesson but one).
exit_intro: Two small checks to finish. Point, say, sign, draw, type or use paper. An adult can scribe your words. You may pass; complete one route, once.

supported.label: Supported
questions: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a higher concentration to a ____ concentration.
A steeper concentration gradient makes diffusion happen ____.
answers: Lower. Particles spread from where they are crowded to where they are few.
Faster. A bigger difference in concentration means a faster net movement.

standard.label: Standard
questions: Complete the definition: diffusion is the ____ movement of particles from a higher to a lower ____.
Name two factors that increase the rate of diffusion.
answers: Net; concentration. Accept net movement of particles down a concentration gradient.
Any two of: a steeper concentration gradient, a higher temperature, a larger surface area, a shorter distance to cross.

stretch.label: Stretch
questions: Explain why a thinner membrane increases the rate of diffusion. Use the word distance.
Explain why warming a gas increases the rate of diffusion. Use the words energy and particles.
answers: A thinner membrane means a shorter distance for particles to cross, so each particle crosses in less time and the rate is higher.
Warmer particles have more energy and move faster, so more of them cross in a given time and the rate rises.
